basic_info.title: A Knowledge Layer in Data-Centric Architectures in the Automotive Industry
basic_info.venue: IC3K 2023 - Volume 2: KEOD (15th International Conference on Knowledge Engineering and Ontology Development), SciTePress, pages 296-303, January 2023

method.technical_details: Proposes a knowledge layer for a data-centric automotive architecture aligned with the DIKW (Data, Information, Knowledge, Wisdom) hierarchy. The knowledge layer uses OWL 2 RL ontologies, Datalog rules, and SPARQL queries to perform knowledge abstraction and decision-making. A generic Tree2Graph/Graph2Tree data conversion bridges the schema-based information layer and the ontology-based knowledge layer via SHACL mappings. An Inference Engine (implemented in C++ with RDFox 6.0 APIs) is deployed both in-vehicle and in the backend (MongoDB middleware). The application scenario reasons over vehicle signal streams (VSSo) to derive daily user trips (DUTo: Fix/StartFix/EndFix, Segment, DailyUserTrip), suggest a business address, and detect traffic jams; reused ontologies include PDMo (Person Data Model) and HLMo (High-level Map). Evaluated via a real-world experiment with a BMW iX between Garching locations.

gap_analysis.whats_missing: It proposes a symbolic semantic/reasoning layer (related to the P1b idea of a semantically-enriched road-network/trajectory representation, but expressed as OWL/RDF ontologies + Datalog rules rather than a learned vector graph). It is not a transformer encoder, has no latent-space RL agent, performs no label-free representation learning, and does not perform GPS map matching (its 'trip inference' is rule-based abstraction of GPS fixes into segments/trips, not snapping GPS to a road network). All decision-making is symbolic logical inference via a reasoner.
gap_analysis.novelty_vs_recombination: real_gap - it occupies a purely symbolic knowledge-representation paradigm, orthogonal to the thesis's learned transformer+RL hybrid, so it shares no methodological pillar and instead motivates the alternative (non-learned) approach to semantic enrichment.

relevance.bmw_relevance: HIGH - this is the most recent published signal of BMW's semantic-data and knowledge-representation strategy direction, co-authored by the thesis interview lead Adel Ayara, and notably mentions trajectory/daily-user-trip inference and future integration of machine learning with reasoning, situating the thesis within BMW's stated roadmap.
